text.p: Here are the highlights from Swiss newspapers on Wednesday: NEUE ZUERCHER ZEITUNG - The European Union Commissioner Hans van den Broek said that Switzerland is responsible for the stalemate of bilateral transportation negotiations because of its inflexibility. - Chemicals group Clariant reported a 26 percent growth in first quarter sales. - Kuoni Travel Group continues its plan for further acquisitions and growth and expects this year's group profit to rise by 20 percent. - Pharmaceuticals group Ares Serono posted extraordinary growth in sales of 20.6 percent to $212 million for the first three months of the year, compared to $175.7 million in the same period of 1996. Net profit doubled by 90 percent to $16.4 million compared to $8.7 million. TAGES ANZEIGER - Time has run out for some 6,300 of the 18,000 Bosnian war refugees in Switzerland who will be sent back to Bosnia today. Hundreds of the refugees would like to stay in Switzerland longer and more than 200 of them have applied for asylum in the United States. - Swiss inflation remained unchanged at 0.5 percent in April. - Swisslog Group plans to increase its 1997 sales to over 400 million Swiss francs with the purchase of Germany's Transnorm System Group. - Oerlikon Buehrle expects its declining operating profit to turn around in 1997. Orders fell by four percent to 824 million Swiss francs in the first quarter, and sales dropped by five percent to 766 million francs. JOURNAL DE GENEVE - Three major health insurance groups in Switzerland - Helsana, Visana and Swica want to increase insurance policy holder's annual deductible to between 600 and 800 francs from 150 francs. -- Zurich Editorial +41 1 631 7340
